assumptions_and_boundaries.name: Iter::new
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The Rust 1.96 target body is exactly the delegation `Iter::new(self)`. The harness verifies that delegation against a narrow exact-vstd iterator contract while leaving the constructor's `NonNull::from_ref`, pointer addition, ZST `without_provenance`, and unsafe raw-pointer representation to a separate source-backed boundary.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: core::ptr::NonNull<T> and raw `end_or_len` iterator representation
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: Rust stores `Iter` as a start pointer and an end pointer or ZST length. The public `iter` body only delegates to `Iter::new`, so the harness uses an opaque lifetime-marker representation and confines pointer/provenance obligations to the constructor boundary.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: spec_slice_iter and IteratorSpec::{remaining,decrease,initial_value_relation}
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The private constructor boundary relates the returned iterator to the exact-vstd iterator vocabulary; the public target postcondition is not assumed directly.

notes: Target body preserves the Rust 1.96 delegation `Iter::new(self)`, adapted only to `Iter::new(slice)` for an explicit Verus receiver. The proof is B, verified modulo the source-backed private constructor/raw-pointer representation boundary. The harness contains no assume_specification, no --no-verify marker, and no public target external_body.
